headword: {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}

definitions.gloss: temple and shrine stamp book; goshuin book
definitions.explanation: A special accordion-fold booklet used to collect goshuin — calligraphic stamps and inscriptions given at Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines as proof of visit and prayer.

examples.japanese: {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}を{買|か}った。
{神社|じんじゃ}で{御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}を{受|う}け{付|つ}けてもらう。
examples.english: To have your goshuin book accepted at a shrine for a stamp.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}のたびに{御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}を{持|も}ち{歩|ある}いて、{各地|かくち}の{寺社|じしゃ}で{御朱印|ごしゅいん}を{集|あつ}めている。
examples.english: I carry my goshuin book with me every trip and collect stamps from temples and shrines around the country.

notes:
A {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう} is typically a beautifully bound accordion-fold (じゃばら) book made of thick Japanese paper. Each page receives a {御朱印|ごしゅいん} — a combination of a red seal stamp and hand-brushed calligraphy with the temple or shrine name and the date of visit. Collecting {御朱印|ごしゅいん} has become a popular hobby and a way to enjoy temple and shrine tourism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}を{持参|じさん}する: to bring one's goshuin book
- {御朱印|ごしゅいん}をもらう: to receive a goshuin stamp
- {御朱印|ごしゅいん}を{集|あつ}める: to collect goshuin stamps
- オリジナル{御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう}: an original goshuin book (sold by specific shrines/temples)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally, {御朱印|ごしゅいん} were given as proof that a pilgrim had copied and offered a sutra. Today they are available to any visitor for a small fee (typically 300-500 yen). Many shrines and temples sell their own unique {御朱印帳|ごしゅいんちょう} with distinctive cover designs.
